text:
Psychological First Aid: The First Five Minutes

The triage app gives you the order to do things in, and this section is about doing them in a way that takes pressure off the person.

Anything that could let someone hurt themselves in the next five minutes takes priority, so get the car keys out of reach and turn the stove off, and move them away from roads and balconies, or pools of water for that matter. Letting them move around is fine, and pacing can help, but keep them from taking more of any substance. If they want to go confront somebody, that can wait. And if they want to leave, have someone go with them. Put any weapons away and keep the person away from crowds and strangers. If they want to post their big revelation about the universe, or message an ex, take the phone.

They're feeling overwhelmed, so dim the lights, and clear out the extra people around them.

Then remind them where they are and what's happening, since a trip can make them lose track of it:

You're in [place], and it's [date/time]. You took [substance, if known], so it'll peak and then change. It's intense right now, but it'll pass, and we can sort out the rest of your life tomorrow.

Have them stop the practice now if that's what brought this on, like meditation or fasting, since their only job now is staying safe. With no drug wearing off on a schedule, there's no telling how long it will last. Once they can eat safely, food and warmth help their body settle.
section: Psychological First Aid: The First Five Minutes
reader: someone sitting with a person on a bad psychedelic trip, or tripping themselves, who needs to know what to do in the first five minutes: dangers first, then the room, then what to say

sentences.s: Psychological First Aid: The First Five Minutes
sentences.payoff: they know what this section covers: the first five minutes of looking after someone
sentences.follows: the section's heading, after the Shadow Work part's welcome

sentences.s: The triage app gives you the order to do things in, and this section is about doing them in a way that takes pressure off the person.
sentences.payoff: they know the triage app sets the order and this section is how to carry it out while taking pressure off the person
sentences.follows: the heading names the first five minutes; this says what the section does in them

sentences.s: Anything that could let someone hurt themselves in the next five minutes takes priority, so get the car keys out of reach and turn the stove off, and move them away from roads and balconies, or pools of water for that matter.
sentences.payoff: they secure whatever could let the person hurt themselves first: keys, stove, roads, balconies, pools
sentences.follows: the first thing to do in the order

sentences.s: Letting them move around is fine, and pacing can help, but keep them from taking more of any substance.
sentences.payoff: they let the person move and pace, but stop them taking more of anything
sentences.follows: still the dangers: movement is fine, more of a substance is not

sentences.s: If they want to go confront somebody, that can wait.
sentences.payoff: they know a confrontation can wait
sentences.follows: what the person may want to do that isn't safe now

sentences.s: And if they want to leave, have someone go with them.
sentences.payoff: they send someone along if the person wants to leave
sentences.follows: the next thing the person may want to do

sentences.s: Put any weapons away and keep the person away from crowds and strangers.
sentences.payoff: they put weapons away and keep the person from crowds and strangers

sentences.s: If they want to post their big revelation about the universe, or message an ex, take the phone.
sentences.payoff: they take the phone before a revelation gets posted or an ex gets messaged
sentences.follows: the last of the things the person may want to do

sentences.s: They're feeling overwhelmed, so dim the lights, and clear out the extra people around them.
sentences.payoff: they dim the lights and clear out the extra people, and know why: the person is overwhelmed
sentences.follows: after the dangers, the room: its two fixes, with the reason (they're overwhelmed)

sentences.s: Then remind them where they are and what's happening, since a trip can make them lose track of it:
sentences.payoff: they know the script that follows is for reminding the person where they are and what's happening, and why: a trip can make them lose track
sentences.follows: after the room is fixed, the reader talks to them

sentences.payoff: the person hears where they are and when
sentences.follows: the script's first two facts, said together

sentences.s: You took [substance, if known], so it'll peak and then change.
sentences.payoff: the person hears what they took and that its effect will peak and then change
sentences.follows: the third fact, with what follows from it ('so')

sentences.s: It's intense right now, but it'll pass, and we can sort out the rest of your life tomorrow.
sentences.payoff: the person hears that the intensity will pass and that their life can wait until tomorrow
sentences.follows: after the facts, what they mean for right now ('but it'll pass') and for the big questions

sentences.s: Have them stop the practice now if that's what brought this on, like meditation or fasting, since their only job now is staying safe.
sentences.payoff: the helper has the person stop the practice that brought the state on, and knows why: staying safe is the only job now
sentences.follows: the other way into this state: a practice instead of a drug, so its own first act

sentences.s: With no drug wearing off on a schedule, there's no telling how long it will last.
sentences.payoff: the helper knows a practice state may last longer than a drug's, with no schedule to count on
sentences.follows: why the practice case needs its own care: the script's 'it'll peak and then change' doesn't hold here

sentences.s: Once they can eat safely, food and warmth help their body settle.
sentences.payoff: they give food and warmth once the person can eat safely, to help their body settle
sentences.follows: the practice case's care, once the practice has stopped

placement: the Psychological First Aid section of the Shadow Work part, before Stillness or Movement? and Get One Human Anchor

opens.first_sentence: Psychological First Aid: The First Five Minutes
opens.why_reading: the heading tells someone looking after a person in a bad state that this is what to do now, in the first five minutes, which is their case; the next line says the triage app sets the order and this section is how to do it without adding pressure

same_point: none: read the section from its heading to Stillness or Movement? for the dangers, the room's two fixes, the reminder of where they are and the practice case; the room paragraph and the pointer to the next sections were cut as repeats of other sections (experiments/t17-room-cut); the practice script's lead-in, script and care are merged here into one paragraph

questions.Q1: PASS: each paragraph opens on its point: the section's job, the first priority, the room's fixes with their reason, what the reminder is for, the practice case's first act
questions.Q2: PASS: every act is the helper's own, with its purpose: the dangers removed, the lights dimmed and the extra people out because they're overwhelmed, the reminder because a trip can make them lose track, the practice stopped because staying safe is the only job
questions.Q3: PASS: which things exactly: keys, stove, roads, balconies, pools, weapons, the phone; the lights, the extra people; place, date and time, the substance; a practice like meditation or fasting; food and warmth
questions.Q4: PASS: no terms a reader wouldn't know; the triage app is linked where it is named
questions.Q5: PASS: each turn has what it turns on: so it'll peak (because of what they took); but it'll pass; since staying safe is the only job; with no drug on a schedule, no telling how long
questions.Q6: PASS: dangers, room, what to say, then the other way into the state with its own care
questions.Q7: PASS: every fact is about the person in front of them now
questions.Q8: PASS: the practice case's act, its timing and its care sit together in one paragraph
questions.Q9: PASS: nothing compressed: the script's facts said in two sentences, with 'so' and 'but' carrying what follows from them

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone? Is each mechanism explained by what it does in the reader's experience (dopamine "for motivation (by showing us what is important to pay attention to)"; DeltaFosB "preventing that learning from really clicking"), not by where it sits or what it looks like ("a chemical blanket", "the slower one underneath")? (E375)
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
question_text.Q9: Is anything compressed? (one step a sentence, the small words that carry the relation, no space before mg)
